proposal.comment: [Playbook] The indemnity runs one way only and Article XIII expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for IP infringement. We have added a standard Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP, legal-compliance, data and wilful-misconduct claims and carved the indemnity out of that disclaimer.

ops.text: Licensor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensee and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Licensor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee's data caused by Licensor; or (d) Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

ops.newText: THE FOREGOING EXCLUSIONS SHALL NOT APPLY TO LICENSOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII
ops.oldText: UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE BY LICENSEE OR ANY THIRD PARTY THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED, RESULTS OR MAY RESULT IN ANY INFRINGEMENT, DEPRIVATION OR VIOLATION OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY, CONSTITUTIONAL, STATUTORY, CONTRACTUAL, COMMON LAW OR OTHER RIGHTS OF ANY PERSON

proposal.summary: Add a Licensor indemnity (IP, law, data, wilful misconduct) and remove the blanket IP-liability disclaimer.

quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless
rationale: The only indemnity runs from Licensee to Licensor and is very broad (any exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business), and Article XIII expressly negates any Licensor liability for IP infringement claims. There is no Vendor IP indemnity at all, which is our walk-away position; we inserted the standard Licensor defence/indemnity and carved it out of the exclusions.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Licensor keeping its platform is fine, but we must retain our own data and cannot pay for customisations that we hold no lasting rights in; we have added a data-ownership sentence and a perpetual, royalty-free licence to Licensee-funded deliverables.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, content and materials provided by Licensee or generated by or for Licensee through use of the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"), and Licensor acquires no rights in Licensee Data other than as strictly necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement. Licensor hereby grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use and modify any customisation, enhancement, front end or other deliverable developed for Licensee and paid for by Licensee under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Confirm Licensee ownership of its own data and add a perpetual licence to customisations Licensee pays for.

quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
rationale: Licensor owning its platform is acceptable, but the Agreement gives us no ownership of, or lasting licence to, customisations and front-end development we pay for under Article VII(b), and it is silent on our own data (which the broad Confidential Information definition and the five-day return obligation could sweep up). That falls short of the fallback perpetual, irrevocable licence, so we added a Licensee Data ownership sentence and a licence-back for Licensee-funded deliverables.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a one-way cap set at one half of amounts paid while our liability is unlimited. We have made the exclusion of indirect damages and the cap mutual, set the cap at 12 months' fees, and placed confidentiality, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; our payment obligations are not capped damages.

ops.newText: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
ops.oldText: IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE TO LICENSEE OR TO ANY THIRD PARTY FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES

ops.newText: (b) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. LICENSEE'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.

proposal.summary: Make the cap and damages exclusion mutual, reset the cap to 12 months' fees and add carve-outs.

quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
rationale: The cap and the consequential-damages exclusion protect only Licensor, and the cap is one half of all amounts paid (well below 6 months' fees), while Licensee's liability is left unlimited and it "assumes all liabilities and risks" (p0029). There are no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnities or IP infringement — Article XIII in fact disclaims Licensor liability for IP infringement. This is walk-away territory; we made the exclusion and cap mutual at 12 months' fees and added the Excluded Claims carve-outs.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need to be able to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in an M&A transaction, and a change of control of our business cannot terminate or re-price the licence; we have added the carve-out and removed the automatic termination trigger.

ops.newText: Licensee may assign this Agreement and its license rights hereunder, in whole or in part, without Licensor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets; any other assignment by Licensee requires Licensor's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.oldText: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.

ops.newText: (a) A Change of Control (as defined below) of Licensee shall not constitute an assignment of this Agreement, shall not require Licensor's consent, and shall not give Licensor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement or Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder.
ops.oldText: (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control. For purposes of the preceding sentence, Licensor will be deemed to have reasonably withheld its consent to a Change of Control if any person or entity who would acquire direct or indirect control (as defined below) of Licensee pursuant to such Change of Control then conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive with a business then conducted by Licensor or any of its Affiliates and/or Licensor reasonably believes that Licensor's interests will be adversely effected by the continuing of this Agreement upon such a Change in Control.

proposal.summary: Add an affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Licensee and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.

quote: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.
rationale: Assignment is blanket-prohibited for Licensee with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Article XX makes the Agreement terminate automatically on our change of control (with a right of first refusal over our own M&A in Article XXII). Both are walk-away items; we added the affiliate/successor carve-out and removed the change-of-control termination trigger.

quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology
rationale: The arrangement is expressly non-exclusive and nothing obliges Licensee to source its requirements from Licensor or to refrain from using other platforms or suppliers, so the preferred position is met.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge is payable by Licensee; fees are usage-based and Article XXIII expressly excludes termination damages. We note Licensor retains fees for trades already executed on termination, which is ordinary accrued consideration rather than an LD.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The grant must reach our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and the licence cannot be cut off for any breach without notice and a cure period; we have limited termination to uncured material breach.

ops.newText: grants to Licensee and its Affiliates and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use
ops.oldText: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use

ops.newText: Upon any material breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder that remains uncured thirty (30) days after Licensor's written notice, the Licensor may terminate this Agreement
ops.oldText: Upon any breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder, the Licensor may immediately terminate this Agreement

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to Licensee's Affiliates and contractors and make revocation subject to uncured material breach.

quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below
rationale: The grant runs to Licensee alone; affiliates and contractors are excluded (use is limited to Licensee employees and outsourcing/service-bureau use is barred), it is non-transferable, and the licence can be revoked immediately for any breach with no notice or cure. That fails the fallback (affiliates on notice, transfer to a successor, revocation only for uncured material breach), so we extended the grant and added a cure period.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: "FIELD OF USE" means, and is limited to, the utilization of the Licensed Technology by the Licensee for the exclusive purpose of fulfilling Spot FX transactions by transmitting market data and orders.
rationale: No covenant restricts the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build; the Field of Use provision is a scope limit on use of the Licensed Technology, not a non-compete, and we address grant scope under LICENSE. We note only that the field-of-use wording is narrow, which we would want confirmed against our intended FX activities.
sectionRef: § I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 36-month term with no exit for us is not something we can sign; we have added a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees. We can discuss moving to 60 days' notice if helpful.

ops.text: Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, in which case Licensor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early termination charge shall be payable.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund.

quote: Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period").
rationale: In a 36-month committed term Licensee has no right to terminate for convenience (termination rights run only to Licensor, on any breach, on change of control or on wind-up), which is our walk-away position. We added a Customer convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund and can fall back to 60 days if needed.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Audits should be no more than once in any 12-month period on 30 days' notice; the notice and cost-sharing here already work, so we have only added the frequency limit.

ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, during normal business hours, and shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to once per 12 months during business hours.

quote: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
rationale: The audit right is written, uses an independent accountant chosen by mutual agreement, is limited to accounting records (no system access) and Licensor bears cost unless a 5% discrepancy is found — all at or better than our position — but there is no cap on how often audits may be requested, so the fallback "once per year" limit fails. Our edit adds only the annual frequency and business-hours limits.

quote: shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A., applicable to contracts entered in and performed entirely within the State of New York
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts in New York City, and no arbitration clause — this is our preferred position.

quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
rationale: Pricing is a fixed volume-band tariff with a rebate in our favour; there is no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation requiring Licensee to extend Licensor terms given to third parties, so the preferred position is met.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
rationale: Fees are purely usage-based on monthly notional volume, with no minimum volume, take-or-pay or shortfall payment; the only fixed amounts are the USD 35,000 initial payment and the USD 2,500 monthly support fee, which are not volume commitments. The 33% share of certain third-party revenues (Article V) is a revenue share rather than a purchase commitment.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A three-year, one-way non-solicit covering every Licensor and Affiliate employee is outside our range; we have made it mutual, limited it to personnel directly involved in this Agreement and reduced it to 12 months, keeping the existing general-advertising carve-out.

ops.newText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the twelve (12) month period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who was directly involved in the performance of this Agreement to leave his or her employment with that party.
ops.oldText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.

proposal.summary: Make the non-solicit mutual, cut it to 12 months and limit it to personnel involved in the Agreement.

quote: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.
rationale: The non-solicit is one-way against us, runs three years post-termination (beyond our 24-month walk-away) and covers every Licensor and Affiliate employee rather than those involved in the services. The general-advertising carve-out is already present, so our edit only makes it mutual, cuts it to 12 months and limits scope to personnel involved in this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot be bound to a seven-year extension exercisable by Licensor alone; renewals should be 12 months and by mutual written agreement, consistent with the mutual-extension language already in this Article.

ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, with any fee increase for a renewal period limited to the lesser of CPI and three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.

proposal.summary: Replace the Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option with 12-month renewals by mutual agreement.

quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
rationale: A seven-year extension exercisable unilaterally by Licensor is worse than an automatic multi-year renewal and gives us no exit window or price protection; it also contradicts the mutual-extension language later in the Article. We reset renewals to 12 months by mutual written agreement with a capped uplift.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to hand everything back; we have added transition assistance for up to six months and return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, with certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (a) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Licensee all Licensee data (including trade, order and account records) in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and return of Licensee data on termination.

quote: Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
rationale: Article XXI runs one way: our licence ends immediately and we must return everything within five days, with no transition assistance and no obligation on Licensor to return our trade and account data. We inserted a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph (six months' assistance, export within 30 days, certified deletion).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no express warranty is not acceptable; we have added a professional-services warranty, a 90-day conformance-to-documentation warranty with repair/replace/refund, and carved these out of the disclaimer.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing disclaimer, Licensor warrants that (a) the Technical Support Services and any other services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Licensed Technology will conform in all material respects to its Documentation; and (c) the Licensed Technology contains no viruses or other malicious code. Licensee's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Licensor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or Licensed Technology.

proposal.summary: Insert an express performance/conformance warranty carved out of the AS IS disclaimer.

quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
rationale: The Agreement is pure "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed, including any warranty that the platform meets its documentation or operates securely — exactly our walk-away position. We inserted the fallback warranty set (workmanlike performance, 90-day conformance to Documentation, no malicious code) with repair/replace/refund, carved out of the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Licensor hosts the platform and our trading data; we have added our standard limits (GL, E&O and cyber) with certificates on request.

ops.text: INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Licensor processes Licensee data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Licensor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a Licensor insurance covenant in the general provisions.

quote: (i) FORCE MAJEURE. Except for the obligations to make payments hereunder, each Party shall be relieved of the obligations hereunder
rationale: There is no insurance covenant anywhere; the only reference to insurance is as a cost we pay under the payment clause. For a vendor hosting the trading platform and our trade data this is a gap, so we inserted a short insurance paragraph (GL, E&O, cyber) in the general provisions; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback.
